subtype: Approach: seeing the crowded evening and redoing the plan [Revision]
passage: Faisal had just started his sums when his mother Afreen came in. "Cousin Hafsa is coming at six." He looked at the clock and at the list, and then he saw the whole evening. Sums, reading, dinner, guests. He crossed out his first plan and wrote a new one: sums first, before dinner. Reading after the guests left. He worked quickly until the doorbell rang. Hafsa stayed for tea and stories. At nine, with the guests gone, Faisal opened his reader and finished the last page. Nothing was left undone.

qa.q: At what time was Cousin Hafsa coming?
What did Faisal feel when he looked at the clock and saw the whole evening?
qa.a: He felt a bit pressed and concerned that there would not be room for everything. He crossed out his first plan and started again.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Faisal use if the guests stay late, and why?
qa.a: He could read a little in the morning before school. That way the reading would not be lost and he would not need to stay up.

qa.q: How might Hafsa feel about visiting while Faisal has homework?
qa.a: Hafsa probably enjoys the tea and stories because Faisal has already finished his sums, so the visit is relaxed for both of them.

grounding: Halfway through his homework a boy notices a cousin is coming at 6 pm and redoes the plan, sums before dinner and reading after the guests leave.
